chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala and Safwan from Mu'awiya said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a person in ihram who killed a wasp. He said, 'If it was by mistake, there is no penalty upon him.' I said, 'But if it was intentional?' He said, 'He feeds a portion of food.'

And there is no harm if a person kills all that he fears from beasts and insects, such as snakes and scorpions and other than that, and no penalty is incumbent upon him. And he does not kill any of them if he did not intend to.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.يُطْعِمُ: He feeds (as a form of expiation)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim in ihram who intentionally kills a wasp?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the fiqh of *kaffarah* (expiation) for a muhrim who kills a wasp, distinguishing between accidental death (no penalty) and intentional killing (requires feeding). It further establishes the principle of *barā'ah* (exemption from penalty) for killing feared beasts and insects, provided the act is not done merely for sport or without cause, reflecting the Shia emphasis on intent (*niyyah*) in ritual purity laws.
